transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

Well, ever since my heart stopped about two and a half years ago, I go out of my way not to think or talk about what happened or anything to do with doctors. My wife finally convinced me to mention it to my cardiologist, which is how I ended up here today. I just really don't like bringing any of it up.
Besides avoiding thoughts and reminders of your heart event, have you been experiencing repeated, unwanted memories or nightmares about it?

Yes, I do, and they come out of nowhere when I'm just sitting in the garden or watching TV. I'll suddenly see myself back on the kitchen floor, hear my wife screaming my name, and my chest tightens up like I'm about to die all over again.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F43.1", "F42", "F32"], but based on this conversation, F42 (obsessive-compulsive disorder) is unlikely because there are no symptoms of obsessions or compulsions described. F32 (depressive episode) is also less likely as there is no mention of persistent low mood, anhedonia, or other depressive symptoms. However, the patient describes clear re-experiencing symptoms (intrusive memories, flashbacks, physiological reactivity to trauma reminders) and active avoidance of trauma-related thoughts and conversations, which are core features of F43.1 (post-traumatic stress disorder). The onset is clearly linked to a major life-threatening event—cardiac arrest—two and a half years ago. Therefore, F43.1 remains the only plausible candidate.
